A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same economic modeling study. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, allowing retained material to be matched despite the changed title, formatting, and appendix organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical equilibrium simulations, including bargaining comparisons and regulatory parameter sweeps in Figures 2 and 4–10.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations and adds numerical robustness checks and joint performance–openness utility landscapes in Figures 8–15.

M1.justification: The original Table 1 game remains, but Appendix C adds models with specialist penalties, logarithmic release costs, and generalist operation costs based on initial rather than final performance. Appendix D.1 expands the generalist's decision from openness alone to jointly choosing initial performance and openness.

E1.justification: v2 adds simulated scenarios with regulatory liability for both developers and with jointly chosen initial performance and openness. The empirical release-data coverage remains unchanged. Appendix D.2 discusses multidimensional performance without evaluating that additional task.

E2.justification: Both versions compare Nash, vertical-monopoly, and egalitarian bargaining and use no-regulation outcomes as references. The new robustness figures use the existing Nash formulation; no additional comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: Existing simulation settings are retained. New utility-landscape evaluations fix the bargaining coefficient at 0.5 or 0.1 with penalty 1 and threshold 0.2, and Appendix C.3 reports alternative-operation-cost checks including a cost coefficient of 1. These are settings for added analyses.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained parameter-sensitivity analysis, Appendix C adds three robustness checks addressing specialist-side liability, logarithmic production costs, and allocation of operation costs. Appendix D.1 also examines the utility landscape when initial performance becomes a decision variable.

E5.justification: The new checklist explicitly states that the experiments have no variability, providing a rationale for the absence of error bars. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; this is a reporting clarification.

E6.justification: v2 adds specialist-penalty outcomes, cost-variant results, and joint-decision utility landscapes. Appendix C.1 reports broader specialist abstention, while C.3 reports slightly higher generalist utility. Existing release-data values and principal equilibrium heatmaps are retained, although Figures 6–7 remove explicitly quoted no-regulation utility values.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition 4 on specialist penalties, Proposition 5 on joint performance–openness optimization, and derivations for alternative cost functions. The original equilibrium proofs and Pareto-regulation propositions remain, with v1's Propositions 4–5 becoming v2's 6–7.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: continuous strategic openness, regulatory effects on bargaining and fine-tuning, and baseline performance determining effective interventions. The appendix extensions do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the earlier cost-and-bargaining explanation with an explicit credible-commitment account of regulation's benefits. v2 also discusses firms tolerating losses, the applicability of fixed initial performance, and mechanisms behind cost robustness. The old Appendix C discussion of total revenue and monetization is omitted.

D1.justification: The new NeurIPS checklist provides a hyperlink to code for reproducing plots and states that simulations require a single CPU and approximately 10–40 minutes. These access and resource details were absent from v1.

R1.justification: A new related-work appendix substantially expands positioning around regulatory thresholds and safety incentives, product versioning and portfolio strategies, and foundation-model supply chains and pricing. Sixteen references are added while the earlier cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, refines model and discussion prose, reorganizes supporting appendices, adds descriptive appendix subsections, and includes a conference checklist. The main section sequence and much of the existing narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts NeurIPS formatting and adds six robustness figure displays and two three-dimensional utility-landscape figures. Existing sensitivity figures become Figures 16–18. Figure 5's threshold legend changes from 1.2 to 1.0; Figures 10/12 and 11/13 reuse plotted panels under different cost-variant labels.

improvement.justification: v2 provides broader robustness coverage, clearer commitment reasoning, and useful code/resource information. However, Proposition 5's new proof asserts a nonnegative determinant under an inequality opposite to that required by its displayed formula. Figures 10–13 also reverse Pareto-improvement versus utility-transfer descriptions relative to their plots and surrounding discussion. These substantive reliability problems in the additions prevent a confident net quality judgment.
